title: How your addon talks to the game.
body: An API—Application Programming Interface—is a set of functions, events, and UI objects Blizzard makes available to addon code. It is the safe vocabulary your Lua uses to ask the game for information or create interface elements. This is the in-game Lua addon API, not the Battle.net web API.
calloutTitle: Think of an API as a menu, not a back door.
calloutBody: Your addon can only do what the game exposes. Some actions are protected during combat, and some information is intentionally restricted.
skuNote: The selected SKU is {sku}. Use Interface {interface} in your TOC, and confirm each function or event for that client.

apiGroups.title: Functions
apiGroups.body: Named calls such as UnitName or CreateFrame that return information or create UI objects.

apiGroups.title: Events
apiGroups.body: Messages the game fires, including PLAYER_LOGIN and PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD.

apiGroups.title: Widgets
apiGroups.body: Frames, buttons, textures, and fonts that make up the on-screen interface.

apiGroups.title: Protected
apiGroups.body: Actions the game blocks during combat so addons cannot automate restricted gameplay.

resources.title: Warcraft Wiki API reference
resources.body: Search functions, events, widgets, examples, and differences between Retail and Classic.

resources.title: In-game API documentation
resources.body: Type /api in WoW for Blizzard's generated function and event reference. Visit the official UI & Macro forum for addon-development guidance and discussion. Do not confuse this with the Battle.net web API.

workflow.title: Name the behavior
workflow.body: I want to know when the player enters the world.

workflow.title: Find the event or function
workflow.body: Search the API reference for PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD.

workflow.title: Check the selected SKU
workflow.body: Confirm availability for Retail, Classic, or the client you are targeting.

workflow.title: Build the smallest test
workflow.body: Try one event or function first, then add behavior after it works.
